balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Accor SA: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Accor SA: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For Accor SA: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Accor SA: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Accor SA: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

mgmtFranchise.title: Management & franchise revenue
mgmtFranchise.content:
Management & franchise revenue is the fee income Accor earns running or licensing hotels it does not own -- base/incentive management fees and franchise royalties, with no owned-hotel capital or occupancy risk.

For Accor SA: this is the core of the post-AccorInvest asset-light thesis -- Accor sold its owned-hotel real estate (AccorInvest) and now earns most of its economics from fees on a network it does not have to fund. A rising share of total revenue means fee income is compounding without matching balance-sheet growth.

What to watch:

  • Management & franchise revenue growing faster than total revenue (mix shift)
  • Whether fee growth tracks net unit growth or RevPAR, or both

network.title: Network size and net unit growth
network.content:
Rooms is the total room count across Accor's managed and franchised network; net unit growth (NUG) is the annual percentage increase in rooms, net of exits and closures -- management's headline expansion KPI.

For Accor SA: NUG is the volume engine behind management & franchise revenue growth in an asset-light model -- fee revenue grows with the network even without Accor spending capital on new hotels. Pipeline (signed but unopened hotels/rooms, not charted here) indicates NUG one to three years out.

What to watch:

  • NUG decelerating below management's mid-single-digit target
  • Rooms growing while RevPAR or occupancy is flat (dilutive growth)

adr.title: RevPAR and average daily rate
adr.content:
RevPAR (revenue per available room) is average daily rate (ADR) multiplied by occupancy -- the standard hotel industry yield metric.

For Accor SA: splitting RevPAR into ADR and occupancy (see the Occupancy chart) shows whether a RevPAR move is a pricing decision or a demand/volume recovery -- they have different implications for the FY2026+ growth path.

What to watch:

  • ADR rising while occupancy falls (pricing-led, volume-fragile)
  • Like-for-like RevPAR growth versus FY2019 as the post-pandemic recovery benchmark

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Accor SA: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Accor SA: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Accor SA: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Accor SA: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Accor SA: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
